text:
maria: Heads up — we've started seeing a bump in Xid 13/31 on eu-west1 between 01:20-01:40 UTC. Pattern looks different from the usual nightly noisy cards.

raj: I saw that on the dashboard too. Link: https://dash.redwood.internal/gpu/xid?range=2h (private)

maria: Summary from the probe notebook I ran:
```
sample_count: 426
xid13: 48
xid31: 32
avg_batch_size_at_errors: 1.4
optype_mix: {decode: 62%, embed: 28%, other: 10%}
cards: a10-48, a10-52
```

maria: Errors spike when decode requests have token_window > 1024 and bursty small batches.

raj: Interesting — earlier Xid 31 we usually saw with tiny batches on older NV cards. But these are A10s. Could be a driver/firmware regression tied to attention kernels.

taylor: @maria can you paste a snippet of the kernel log from the node that shows Xid 13? dmesg or /var/log/kern.log is fine.

maria: pasted logs: 
```
[Jan 20 01:22:14] NVRM: Xid (13): GPU has fallen off the bus.
[Jan 20 01:22:14] NVRM: Xid (31): Uncorrectable ECC error on memory channel 3
[Jan 20 01:22:14] NVRM: GPU 0: GPU-1234abcd - a10-48
```

maria: Node shows ECC counters rising then a bus fault.

raj: Two hypotheses: (1) transient PCIe flakiness under certain decode kernel paths, (2) a specific tenant workload that triggers a bad compilation path.

taylor: Can we correlate to tenant op mix? @infra-bot can you pull the tenant_id for requests hitting that GPU around 01:20-01:25?

infra-bot: tenant correlation query complete. Top tenants in window: tenant-alpha (48%), tenant-gamma (21%), tenant-internal (14%). Attached sample request IDs: r-9fa3, r-9fa4, r-9fa7.

maria: tenant-alpha is running a modified decode kernel (prompt engineering plugin) in prod-canary.

raj: That narrows it — their canary was rolled at 00:55 UTC. Rollback at 02:10 seemed to reduce the rate.

taylor: What about firmware/driver churn? Any recent node reboots or driver upgrades in eu-west1 around midnight?

infra-bot: Fleet events: driver 525.85 -> 525.85-rc1 rolled on 01:00 UTC to ~12% of nodes in eu-west1.

maria: Aha. So canary + driver rc could be the interaction. Both are low probability alone. Together they line up with start and stop windows.

raj: Action plan: 1) Quarantine the affected card IDs, drain politely (no hard kill), 2) Reproduce on staging with driver-rc + tenant-alpha's request corpus, 3) If reproducible escalate to NVIDIA and tenant team.

taylor: Agreed. For the drain: `kubectl drain node/gpu-eu-west1-028 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300` and set node-level tag `xid-investigation=true` so autoscaler doesn't replace immediately.

maria: I'll schedule a maintenance drain now for 028 and 031 (the two listed in the probe). Doing a rolling drain so we keep capacity.

maria: Also added a temporary routing policy: prefer us-east as fallback for tenant-alpha real-time decode until we identify root cause.

raj: Cost note — fallback to us-east increases cross-region egress and SLO risk. Approx estimate: +$0.6k/day if sustained. Flagging finance impact.

taylor: For reproduction: @raj can you spin up a staging pool with driver-rc, run the tenant-alpha corpus with sequence_len=2048 and batch_size sweep [1,2,4] and capture `perf` & `nv-hostengine` logs?

raj: On it. I'll also add elevated debug for the attention kernels and capture GPU telemetry (smaps, nvml counters).

maria: If we confirm interaction, mitigation options: pin drivers to stable for production (rollback RC), throttle tenant-alpha canary, or add a runtime kernel patch if NVIDIA has a fix.

taylor: Also check for shared ECC growth across cards in the same chassis — if multiple cards in one host show ECC drift, schedule early replacement.

maria: Noted. Current ECC delta over 24h on node-028 is +190 corrected errors, which is borderline. I'll open a hardware ticket for vendor to run a thermal/profile check.

raj: For visibility: creating incident doc and slack incident channel if we escalate. If anyone sees another region show the same driver-rc + canary overlap, ping here.

maria: Quick ephemeral test result: rolled back tenant-alpha canary on a subset and Xid rate dropped ~85% in 20 mins. Suggests workload trigger is primary.

taylor: Good - that helps prioritize. Next steps checklist: reproduce in staging, hold driver rollout, hardware check for nodes with ECC delta > 150, and compute cost delta if routing policy persists.

sre-oncall: I'll take the hardware ticket and brood over maintenance windows. Marking this thread for postmortem if we end up replacing cards. :mag: 

maria: Thanks all — I'll update the ticket and attach the probe notebook and logs. :thumbsup:
